title: Utah AI sandbox launches new health care pilots — with question marks
key_facts: Utah announced three new pilots last week: AI that refills prescriptions for chronic conditions, writes initial acne prescriptions and offers virtual physical therapy.

Zach Boyd, director of Utah's Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy (OAIP), spoke at the ADAPT conference in Santa Fe, New Mexico, on Thursday (15 Oct 2026) and said the state is working on evidentiary standards, governance guidance and a liability bill.

The sandbox lets companies test technology in exchange for regulatory relief and state oversight; an earlier pilot with Doctronic lets AI refill certain prescriptions with clinician oversight, and the Utah Medical Licensing Board opposed it in an April letter before forming a weekly working group with regulators.
Utah removed some drugs, including butalbital and flecainide, from its list of 190 drugs AI may refill after scrutiny from the licensing board.

Pilot companies must carry special liability insurance and not waive liability; Boyd says long term the vendor should be held directly liable, and he hopes a liability bill is unveiled this month or next, starting a multi-year process.

Whether the FDA will regulate the pilot technology is open: it generally requires pre-market authorization for software that treats or diagnoses patients; Boyd hopes for a unified pathway with federal regulators.
Six independent evaluators, including the Coalition for Health AI and the Stanford Clinical Excellence Research Center, assess companies' technical claims; future pilots must contract with one.
quote_evidence: Through the AI sandbox, Utah has allowed companies to test new technologies in exchange for regulatory relief and state oversight.
But Utah regulators are still mulling over how the state should split legal liability between AI and the human clinicians who oversee them if patients are harmed.
Another big question facing Utah’s sandbox is whether the Food and Drug Administration will regulate pilot AI technology.
why_it_matters_hint: Utah is letting AI prescribe and treat under state supervision while key questions on liability and FDA oversight remain unanswered.
event_date: Pilots announced the week of 5 Oct 2026 (exact day not stated); Boyd's remarks Thursday 15 Oct 2026.
